items.title: NRL Late Mail: Round 21 - Panthers lose Edwards
items.snippet:
A blow for the Panthers ahead of Thursday night's Battle of the West with gun fullback Dylan Edwards ruled out due to a head cut.

Edwards suffered the gash during last week's loss to the Broncos that required 10 stitches.

The loss of David Fifita to suspension and Cameron Murra
items.body_excerpt:
A blow for the Panthers ahead of Thursday night's Battle of the West with gun fullback Dylan Edwards ruled out due to a head cut.

Edwards suffered the gash during last week's loss to the Broncos that required 10 stitches.

The loss of David Fifita to suspension and Cameron Murray and Tallis Duncan to injury has forced the Rabbitohs into a major reshuffle ahead of their crucial clash with the Storm.

Goalkicking centre Latrell Siegwalt lines up for his career seventh game while Lachlan Hubner starts at lock and Liam Le Blanc is also set for a call-up.

Cowboys coach Todd Payten has recalled experienced playmaker Jake Clifford to partner Tom Dearden in the halves for a bumper showdown against the Broncos at a sold-out Queensland Country Bank Stadium.

See all the late mail, official team news and updates for Round 21 of the 2026 NRL Telstra Premiership competition.

Eels: Star playmaker Mitch Moses plays just his 13th game for the season as he returns from a corked thigh to take on Blues halves partner Nathan Cleary. Five-eighth Ronald Volkman suffered a head knock against the Roosters before the bye but has cleared the concussion protocols to take his place. Luca Moretti also returns from a concussion on the bench. No changes in Wednesday's update with Will Penisini remaining in the squad and a chance to return from a case of Osteitis Pubis that has sidelined him since Round 9.

Panthers: Fullback Dylan Edwards has dropped out of the side as he continues his recovery from a head cut suffered last week and been replaced Thomas Jenkins. The shuffle sees Paul Alamoti push to the wing and Izack Tago come in at centre. Jaxen Edgar has been added to the bench. Edwards suffered a head cut that required 10 stitches post-match in last week's loss to the Broncos. Mitch Kenny (leg) could still be a couple of weeks away so Freddy Lussick will do the job as starting hooker for the 11th straight game. Winger Brian To'o needs one try to bring up a century of tries in the NRL.

Knights: Veteran centre Dane Gagai has succumbed to calf tightness so the versatile Fletcher Hunt will start in the No.3 jersey. Cody Hopwood returns from a calf injury on the bench while Sandon Smith is named in No.14 and will be hoping for game time this week after going unused against the Sharks. The Knights have won their last five games at McDonald Jones Stadium.

items.snippet:
The Rabbitohs have been dealt a double blow with inspirational skipper Cameron Murray and gun centre/back-rower Tallis Duncan both facing stints on the sideline.

items.body_excerpt:
The Rabbitohs have been dealt a double blow with inspirational skipper Cameron Murray and gun centre/back-rower Tallis Duncan both facing stints on the sideline.

Murray sustained a grade two calf strain against the Raiders and is expected to be sidelined for 3-4 weeks while Duncan is facing 2-3 weeks out with a hamstring strain.

Champion centre Latrell Mitchell has undergone further investigations and consultation with a specialist neurologist last week.

Mitchell is trying to overcome complex nerve damage that initially created complications with a lower back injury, and now a calf issue in his left leg. He remains a week-to-week proposition as to a return to the field of play.

Penrith will be without star fullback Dylan Edwards for Thursday's clash with the Eels as he continues to recover from a nasty gash suffered last week.

The cut to Edwards' head required 10 stitches post-game and he dropped out of the Panthers' side in Wednesday's 24-hour team update.

Meanwhile, scans have revealed Sea Eagles superstar Tom Trbojevic suffered a low-grade strain to his right hamstring and faces at least four weeks on the sideline.

After missing eight games with a serious injury to his left hamstring, Turbo returned in Round 16 and had averaged 151 metres per game across four matches before playing just 21 minutes on Sunday.

"Tom will not play in Sunday’s game against the Sharks at 4 Pines Park and will be reassessed after the team’s Round 22 bye," the Sea Eagles said in a statement.

A devastating blow for Raiders back-rower Hudson Young as he suffered a ruptured Achilles against the Rabbitohs on Saturday, just 24 hours after Storm winger Will Warbrick had his season ended by the same injury.

Young collapsed to the turf with no-one around him in the 55th minute and had to be assisted from the field. He finished the day on the bench with his leg in a moon boot.

The Raiders confirmed on Monday that Young would undergo surgery on Tuesday and would miss the remainder of the season, including the World Cup.

Englishman Matty Nicholson has been named on the Raiders' extended bench for the first time this season after recovering from shoulder surgery.

Meanwhile, the Storm confirmed on Saturday that Warbrick had sustained a ruptured Achilles tendon and would undergo surgery.

On a positive note the Storm get halfback Jahrome Hughes back from a hamstring injury for their clash with the Rabbitohs.

items.body_excerpt:
The Panthers are out to steady the ship when they face fierce rivals Parramatta in the latest edition of the Western Sydney derby on Thursday night.

Penrith have battled a rocky patch in recent weeks, winning just one of their past four games to see their lead at the top of the table diminish to just two points.

With the Warriors and Roosters breathing down their necks, the Panthers need a win to maintain their grip on the minor premiership.

It won't be easy, however, with Parramatta well rested after last week's bye and eager to keep their finals hopes alive.

The Eels likely need to win six of their last seven games to sneak into the top eight but anything is possible with halfback Mitchell Moses pulling the strings.

The skipper will go face to face with his NSW halves partner on Thursday night in a battle between two of the game's playmakers.

Eels: Star playmaker Mitch Moses plays just his 13th game for the season as he returns from a corked thigh to take on Blues halves partner Nathan Cleary. Five-eighth Ronald Volkman suffered a head knock against the Roosters before the bye but has cleared the concussion protocols to take his place. Luca Moretti also returns from a concussion on the bench. No changes in Wednesday's update with Will Penisini remaining in the squad and a chance to play his first game since Round 9 having recovered from Osteitis Pubis.

Panthers: Fullback Dylan Edwards has dropped out of the side as he continues his recovery from a nasty head cut suffered last week and been replaced Thomas Jenkins. The shuffle sees Paul Alamoti push to the wing and Izack Tago come in at centre. Jaxen Edgar has been added to the bench. Edwards suffered a head cut that required 10 stitches post-match in last week's loss to the Broncos. Mitch Kenny (leg) could still be a couple of weeks away so Freddy Lussick will do the job as starting hooker for the 11th straight game.

items.title: NRLW Casualty Ward: Meakes, Elliston out for season
items.snippet:
Scans have confirmed the worst fears of Knights fans, with skipper Yasmin Meakes out for the season after suffering a ruptured ACL.

The NSW and Jillaroos star suffered the injury after falling awkwardly in a tackle midway through the first half of Newcastle's win over the Dragon
items.body_excerpt:
Scans have confirmed the worst fears of Knights fans, with skipper Yasmin Meakes out for the season after suffering a ruptured ACL.

The NSW and Jillaroos star suffered the injury after falling awkwardly in a tackle midway through the first half of Newcastle's win over the Dragons.

Meakes will undergo reconstructive surgery before commencing a structured rehabilitation program under the guidance of the club’s medical and high-performance staff.

The injury also rules the Jillaroos forward out of the upcoming Rugby League World Cup.

Meakes joins fullback Lilly-Ann White is expected to miss up to eight weeks after suffering a syndesmosis injury against the Sharks in Round 1 on the sidelines.

Newcastle will also be without Evie Jones (hamstring), Ella-Jaye Harrison-Leaunoa (ACL) and rugby Sevens recruit Damita Betham (shoulder) for the remainder of the season.

A huge blow for the Titans with star prop Jess Elliston ruled out for the rest of the season with a knee injury suffered in Round 1 against the Roosters.

The veteran of 49 NRLW games will require surgery after scans confirmed a Grade 3 MCL tear for the Origin and Jillaroos forward.

Elliston will miss the remainder of the Titans' campaign and is also unavailable for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup.

Fellow Titan Destiny Mino-Sinapati will spend the next month continuing to rehab her MCL injury sustained in Round 1 as she looks to make her return later this season.

Centre Georgia Grey will miss the next month after undergoing surgery for a fractured finger suffered in Sunday's record 50-12 win against the Eels.

Meanwhile, Sharks captain Tiana Penitani Gray remains sidelined with a quad strain that ruled her out of what would have been her 50th NRLW match in Round 3 against the Bulldogs.

Eels lock Kennedy Cherrington is expected to miss a number of weeks after suffering a facial fracture in the loss to the Dragons in Round 2. The club reported that the Māori All Stars representative had suffered a left orbital fracture, with a return to play timeframe still to be established.

Second-rower Chloe Jackson has also been sidelined for the Eels with a rib complaint.

Joining them on the sidelines is Rysh'e Fa'amausili , who suffered a head knock and was not named for their Round 4 match against the Warriors.

Roosters interchange forward Macie Carlile has been sidelined with a knee injury.
